definitions: A type of thematic map that uses symbols of different sizes to represent different values or quantities of a particular phenomenon in various areas.
A map where the size of a symbol (e.g., a circle, square) is proportional to the value of the attribute it represents at a given location.
examples: The cartographer created a graduated symbol map to show population density.
Analyzing the graduated symbol map revealed regional disparities.
A graduated symbol map is effective for visualizing quantitative data.
